what_it_does: Quantum computers are fragile: qubits (quantum bits) lose their state quickly, so they need error correction. Standard error-correction codes assume qubits are connected in dense grids where any two can interact instantly. Real quantum hardware has sparse connectivity—qubits can only directly interact with nearby neighbors. QECC-Synth automates the translation: it inserts extra qubits (ancillas) to bridge distances, then solves a global optimization problem to find the best placement and routing for these bridges. The approach is automatic, handles multiple error-correction codes (surface code, color code, etc.), and requires no manual architecture-specific redesign.
